roleplays.title: Job Interview
roleplays.description: Practice a first-round interview for a product or operations role.
roleplays.workplaceContext: A hiring manager asks about your experience and motivation.
roleplays.userGoal: Answer with situation, action and result.
roleplays.openingLine: Thanks for joining today. Could you start by telling me a little about yourself?

promptVariants.title: Tell me about yourself
promptVariants.openingLine: Thanks for joining today. Could you start by telling me a little about yourself?
promptVariants.userGoal: Give a short career story: role, proof point and why this role.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Use present, past and future: who you are now, what experience proves it and why this role is next.
suggestedPhrases: Currently, I focus on...
Before that, I built experience in...
That is why this role feels like a strong next step.

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This interview answer should sound like a concise career story, not a full biography.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You framed your background around relevant experience instead of listing every past role.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Close by linking your background to why this role is the right next step.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: Currently, I work in operations where I focus on improving cross-team workflows. Before that, I built experience coordinating customer feedback and turning it into clear priorities. That mix of communication and execution is why this role feels like a strong next step for me.

promptVariants.title: Why this role?
promptVariants.openingLine: What interests you most about this role and our company?
promptVariants.userGoal: Link your motivation to the role and your next step.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Avoid a generic answer. Mention one role requirement and one reason it fits your experience.
suggestedPhrases: What interests me most is...
This connects well with my experience in...
I am looking for a role where I can...

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This interview answer should connect your motivation to the role requirements and the company.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You linked your interest to the role instead of giving a generic motivation answer.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Name one specific part of the role or company that matches your experience.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: What interests me most is that this role combines customer insight with cross-functional execution. That connects well with my experience turning feedback into clear product priorities, and I am looking for a role where I can keep growing in that direction.

promptVariants.title: Difficult situation
promptVariants.openingLine: Can you describe a difficult work situation and how you handled it?
promptVariants.userGoal: Use situation, action, result and one lesson learned.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Keep the problem short, spend most of the answer on what you did and end with the result.
suggestedPhrases: The situation was challenging because...
I took responsibility for...
The result was that we...

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This interview answer should stay structured around situation, action, result and one short lesson.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You focused on your actions under pressure, which is what interviewers want to hear here.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: End with one clear lesson learned so the example sounds complete.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: The situation was challenging because two teams disagreed on the launch timeline. I took responsibility for aligning the open issues, setting a shorter decision meeting and clarifying the owner for each action. As a result, we launched on time, and I learned that calm structure matters most when pressure is high.

suggestedPhrases: In my previous role, I was responsible for...
The main challenge was...
As a result, we improved...
followUpPrompts: That sounds useful. Can you give me one specific example of a result you created?
What would your previous manager say is your strongest communication skill?

feedback.summary: Your answer is professional and easy to follow. The next improvement is to add one specific result.
improvements: Close with why the role fits your next step
feedback.suggestedRewrite: In my previous role, I coordinated weekly customer feedback reviews. The main challenge was turning scattered notes into clear product priorities. I created a simple scoring system, and as a result, the team reduced follow-up time by about 20%.

roleplays.title: Meeting Practice
roleplays.description: Practice joining a weekly project meeting and giving a useful update.
roleplays.workplaceContext: Your team needs a quick update on progress and blockers.
roleplays.userGoal: Share progress, blocker and the support you need.
roleplays.openingLine: Let's start with your update. What changed since our last meeting?

promptVariants.title: Status update
promptVariants.openingLine: Let's start with your update. What changed since our last meeting?
promptVariants.userGoal: Share progress, blocker and the support you need.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Use three short parts: progress, blocker and next step.
suggestedPhrases: Since our last meeting, I completed...
The main blocker right now is...
My next step is to...

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This meeting answer should organize progress, blocker and next step in a short update.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You gave the meeting a clear progress update instead of speaking generally.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Name the blocker and the next step so the team knows what support you need.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: Since our last meeting, I completed the first draft and shared it with the team. The main blocker right now is the missing customer data, so my next step is to confirm the owner and follow up by Friday.

promptVariants.title: Clarify deadline
promptVariants.openingLine: The timeline looks tight. What deadline or dependency do you need clarified?
promptVariants.userGoal: Ask one clear question without sounding defensive.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Name the dependency, explain the risk briefly and ask for a clear owner or date.
suggestedPhrases: Could we clarify the deadline for...
The dependency I am waiting on is...
To stay on track, I need...

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This meeting answer should clarify the deadline or dependency without sounding defensive.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You asked for clarification in a calm, professional way.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Name the specific dependency and ask for one clear owner or date.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: Could we clarify the deadline for the customer data review? The dependency I am waiting on is the final approval from finance. To stay on track, I need a confirmed owner and date by tomorrow.

promptVariants.title: Challenge decision
promptVariants.openingLine: I think we should move forward with the current plan. Do you see any risks?
promptVariants.userGoal: Challenge politely with one risk and one alternative.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Start by acknowledging the plan, then add your concern and suggest a practical next step.
suggestedPhrases: I understand the reason for that decision.
One risk I see is...
Could we also consider...

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This meeting answer should challenge the decision politely while offering a constructive alternative.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You raised the risk respectfully instead of rejecting the plan.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Pair the risk with one practical alternative or next step.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: I understand the reason for that decision. One risk I see is that we may not have enough time for customer validation. Could we also consider a shorter pilot before committing to the full plan?

promptVariants.title: Polite disagreement
promptVariants.openingLine: I think we should skip the customer review and launch this week. Does anyone disagree?
promptVariants.userGoal: Disagree politely, explain one risk and ask for a short clarification.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Acknowledge the goal, use one softener and ask a focused question before suggesting a safer next step.
suggestedPhrases: I see the goal, but I am concerned about...
Could we clarify whether...
A safer next step might be...

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This meeting answer should disagree respectfully while asking for one useful clarification.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You disagreed without sounding confrontational, which keeps the meeting productive.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Make the clarification question specific so the team knows what decision is needed.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: I see the goal of launching quickly, but I am concerned that skipping the customer review could create avoidable issues. Could we clarify whether the review can be shortened instead of removed? A safer next step might be a same-day review with only the highest-risk points.

suggestedPhrases: Since our last meeting, I completed...
The main blocker is...
The next step is...
followUpPrompts: Thanks. What support do you need from the team before the next meeting?
If the blocker continues, what backup plan would you suggest?

feedback.summary: The update is clear, but it needs a sharper ask at the end.
feedback.suggestedRewrite: Since our last meeting, I finished the first draft and shared it with design. The main blocker is that I need final pricing details from finance. Could we confirm who owns that by tomorrow?

roleplays.title: Presentation Practice
roleplays.description: Practice a short presentation about a business idea or project update.
roleplays.workplaceContext: You are presenting a recommendation to leaders.
roleplays.userGoal: Open clearly and move smoothly between points.
roleplays.openingLine: Before you begin, what should we pay attention to during your presentation?

promptVariants.title: Opening agenda
promptVariants.openingLine: Before you begin, what should we pay attention to during your presentation?
promptVariants.userGoal: Open with topic, structure and the decision you need.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Start with the purpose, preview the structure and tell the audience what decision or takeaway matters.
suggestedPhrases: Today I will cover three points...
The main decision we need is...
By the end, I want you to understand...

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This presentation answer should set the topic, structure and decision clearly at the start.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You gave the audience a clear reason to listen before going into details.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: State the decision or takeaway you want before listing the presentation points.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: Today I will cover three points: the customer problem, the proposed solution and the decision we need. By the end, I want you to understand why a small pilot is the safest next step.

promptVariants.title: Smooth transition
promptVariants.openingLine: You finished your first point. How would you move naturally into the second point?
promptVariants.userGoal: Connect the previous point to the next business reason.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Avoid saying only 'next'. Link the ideas with a phrase like 'This matters because...' or 'That leads to...'.
suggestedPhrases: This leads to the next point...
The reason this matters is...
Let me connect this to...

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This presentation answer should connect the previous point to the next business reason.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You used signposting that helps the audience follow the structure.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Explain why the transition matters instead of only saying what comes next.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: This leads to the next point: execution risk. The reason this matters is that even a strong idea needs a realistic rollout plan, so let me connect the recommendation to the timeline.

promptVariants.title: Handle challenge
promptVariants.openingLine: I understand the recommendation, but why should we prioritize this now?
promptVariants.userGoal: Answer calmly with evidence and one next step.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Acknowledge the concern first, then give one reason, one proof point and a small next step.
suggestedPhrases: That is a fair concern.
The reason I still recommend this is...
A low-risk next step would be...

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This presentation answer should acknowledge the challenge, give evidence and propose a practical next step.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You responded to skepticism calmly instead of becoming defensive.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Add one proof point before recommending the next step.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: That is a fair concern. The reason I still recommend this is that the customer feedback points to a clear opportunity, and a low-risk next step would be a two-week pilot before a larger investment.

promptVariants.title: Audience question
promptVariants.openingLine: One audience member asks: How do we know this recommendation is worth the extra work?
promptVariants.userGoal: Answer briefly, give one reason and return to the next step.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Acknowledge the question, answer with one business reason and close with what you recommend next.
suggestedPhrases: That is a fair question.
The main reason is...
The next step I recommend is...

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This presentation answer should handle the audience question directly and return to a clear recommendation.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You acknowledged the question before answering, which keeps the tone confident and respectful.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Close with the next step so the audience knows what decision or action you want.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: That is a fair question. The main reason this is worth the extra work is that it reduces launch risk before we commit more resources. The next step I recommend is a short pilot so we can test the impact with a smaller group first.

suggestedPhrases: Today I will cover three points...
This leads to the second point...
The key takeaway is...
followUpPrompts: What is the one decision you want the audience to make after your presentation?
How would you answer if someone challenges your recommendation?

feedback.summary: The presentation has a strong opening. Add clearer signposting before each main point.
feedback.suggestedRewrite: Today I will cover the customer problem, the proposed solution and the next decision we need. The key takeaway is that we can test this with a small pilot before making a larger investment.

roleplays.title: Sales Call
roleplays.description: Practice a consultative sales conversation with a potential customer.
roleplays.workplaceContext: A prospect likes the idea but questions the cost.
roleplays.userGoal: Ask about pain, confirm value and handle price calmly.
roleplays.openingLine: I understand what your product does, but I'm not sure the price makes sense for us.

promptVariants.title: Price concern
promptVariants.openingLine: I understand what your product does, but I'm not sure the price makes sense for us.
promptVariants.userGoal: Acknowledge price, ask one question and link value to impact.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Do not defend the price immediately. First learn what the problem currently costs them.
suggestedPhrases: That makes sense. Can I ask what this problem currently costs you?
Before we discuss price, what outcome would make this worthwhile?
If we could reduce that cost, would the investment feel different?

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This sales answer should acknowledge the price concern before connecting cost to business impact.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You treated the price concern as a discovery moment instead of defending immediately.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Ask what the current problem costs before explaining the value of the solution.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: That makes sense. Before we discuss price, can I ask what this problem currently costs your team in time or missed opportunities? If we could reduce that cost, the investment may feel easier to evaluate.

promptVariants.title: Budget value
promptVariants.openingLine: The value is clear, but we do not have budget for another tool right now.
promptVariants.userGoal: Clarify budget limits and tie value to one measurable result.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Acknowledge the budget limit, ask how budget is approved and connect the decision to measurable impact.
suggestedPhrases: I understand budget is a real constraint.
How are budget decisions usually approved?
Could we compare the cost with the impact you want?

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This sales answer should respect the budget limit and connect value to one measurable business result.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You treated budget as a real constraint and kept the conversation consultative.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Ask how budget is approved before suggesting a value comparison.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: I understand budget is a real constraint. How are budget decisions usually approved on your team? If it helps, we can compare the cost with the impact you want before deciding whether this belongs in the budget.

promptVariants.title: Timing concern
promptVariants.openingLine: This looks interesting, but I don't think this is the right time for us.
promptVariants.userGoal: Explore timing and suggest a smaller next step.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Ask what would need to change for this to become a priority, then suggest a low-pressure next action.
suggestedPhrases: What would need to change for this to become a priority?
Would a smaller pilot be easier to evaluate now?
Can we agree on a low-pressure next step?

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This sales answer should explore timing without pressuring the prospect to decide now.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You kept the timing objection low-pressure and focused on the buyer's priorities.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Ask what would need to change before suggesting a smaller next step.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: What would need to change for this to become a priority? If now is not the right time, would a smaller pilot be easier to evaluate, or should we agree on a low-pressure next step for later?

promptVariants.title: Existing tool
promptVariants.openingLine: We already use another tool for this, so I'm not sure we need to change anything.
promptVariants.userGoal: Respect their setup and uncover one gap.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Do not attack their current tool. Compare outcomes, workflow friction or missed opportunities.
suggestedPhrases: It's good that you already have a process in place.
What works well with your current tool?
Where does the current workflow still create friction?

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This sales answer should respect the current tool while uncovering one workflow gap.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You respected the current setup before asking about gaps or friction.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Ask what works well first, then uncover one specific workflow gap.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: It's good that you already have a process in place. What works well with your current tool, and where does the current workflow still create friction for your team?

suggestedPhrases: Could you tell me more about...
What would the impact be if...
It sounds like the main concern is...
followUpPrompts: Before we talk about price, what question would you ask to understand the customer's real concern?
How would you connect the product value back to the customer's own words?

feedback.summary: You acknowledged the concern well. Ask one more discovery question before defending the product.
improvements: Ask about current cost of the problem
Tie value to the customer's words
feedback.suggestedRewrite: That makes sense. Before we talk about price, could you tell me what this problem currently costs your team in time or missed opportunities?

roleplays.title: Workplace Small Talk
roleplays.description: Practice short workplace conversations before meetings or with new colleagues.
roleplays.workplaceContext: You join a call early with a new colleague.
roleplays.userGoal: Start naturally and keep it professional.
roleplays.openingLine: Hi, I don't think we've met before. How's your day going?

promptVariants.title: Quick introduction
promptVariants.openingLine: Hi, I don't think we've met before. How's your day going?
promptVariants.userGoal: Introduce yourself, your role and one simple work question.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Keep it light: greeting, name, role and one easy question about their work or project.
suggestedPhrases: Nice to meet you. I work on the product team.
I'm Kevin, and my role is focused on customer growth.
What team or project are you working with?

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This small talk answer should introduce you warmly, mention your role and ask one light professional question.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You kept the introduction warm, brief and work-appropriate.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Mention your role and ask one easy professional question to keep the conversation moving.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: Nice to meet you. I'm Kevin, and my role is focused on customer growth. What team or project are you working with?

promptVariants.title: Friendly follow-up
promptVariants.openingLine: I'm doing well, thanks. I've been busy with this project all week.
promptVariants.userGoal: Respond naturally and ask a friendly work question.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Show interest in the work, not private details. A good follow-up keeps the conversation moving.
suggestedPhrases: That sounds like a busy week.
What part of the project has been most interesting?
I hope the work is going smoothly.

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This small talk answer should respond naturally and ask a friendly work-focused follow-up question.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You showed interest in the other person's work without becoming too personal.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Ask one follow-up question about the project or team to keep the conversation natural.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: That sounds like a busy week. What part of the project has been most interesting so far? I hope the work is going smoothly.

promptVariants.title: Move to meeting
promptVariants.openingLine: It was nice chatting. I think everyone is joining now.
promptVariants.userGoal: Close the chat politely and move to the meeting topic.
promptVariants.coachingNote: Use a short bridge phrase like 'Shall we get started?' or 'Maybe we can begin with the agenda.'
suggestedPhrases: It was nice chatting before the meeting.
Shall we get started with the agenda?
Maybe we can begin with the first topic.

feedbackGuidance.summaryHint: This small talk answer should close the chat politely and move into the meeting topic.
feedbackGuidance.strengthFocus: You transitioned from friendly small talk into the meeting without sounding abrupt.
feedbackGuidance.improvementFocus: Use a bridge phrase like 'Shall we get started?' before naming the agenda.
feedbackGuidance.suggestedRewrite: It was nice chatting before the meeting. Shall we get started with the agenda? Maybe we can begin with the first topic.

suggestedPhrases: Nice to meet you.
How long have you been working on this project?
That sounds interesting.
followUpPrompts: What friendly follow-up question would you ask to keep the conversation natural?
How would you politely move from small talk into the meeting topic?

feedback.summary: The conversation sounds friendly and appropriate. Add one follow-up question to keep it moving.
improvements: Use the person's name if you know it
feedback.suggestedRewrite: Nice to meet you. My day is going well, thanks. How long have you been working with this team?
